{
  "description": "A family-aware diagnostic adapter for Self-EvolveRec that measures the trained HSTU recommender through the host ModelView interface. It returns measured metrics with explicit definitions and builds an interpretation prompt grounded in those measurements. This is a supplied design description, not a linked paper.",
  "motivation": "Make model diagnosis reliable across architecture changes while preventing fabricated signals, padding errors, and confusion between training diagnostics and the benchmark selection metric.",
  "implementation_notes": "Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use view.model as the actual trained network and retain item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, and review_data compatibility. Process batches shaped B × L, excluding padding from metric denominators. For sequence readout, select the final nonpadding position using position indices, never count−1 on left-padded histories. Suitable diagnostics include history lengths, item-frequency concentration, embedding norms, and positive-versus-negative score margins measured from supplied batches. Mark unavailable measurements explicitly; never infer review content, ratings, product attributes, or simulator traits. Preserve the model's prior training mode after probing. Keep one independently trained HSTU model/checkpoint per category and consistent checkpoint/predictor architecture. Model selection remains the host's macro-average validation HR@10 across all four categories; diagnostic scores do not replace it.",
  "pseudocode": "class DiagnosisProbe(view, device):
  run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save view.model.training
    set model to evaluation mode
    initialize metric accumulators
    without gradients:
      for (_, sequence, positive, negative) in train_loader:
        move tensors to device
        compute nonpadding masks and history lengths
        features = view.log2feats(sequence)
        obtain aligned positive and negative scores through view.predict_score
        accumulate score margins and pairwise accuracy on valid target positions
        when sequence readout is needed, gather the maximum nonpadding position index
      measure supported embedding and public-history statistics
    restore previous model mode
    return {metrics: aggregated measurements, metric_definitions: definitions including denominators and limitations}

function diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
  include measured metrics and their definitions
  distinguish observations from hypotheses and unavailable evidence
  request HSTU-compatible, single-model improvement hypotheses
  state that host macro validation HR@10 determines selection",
  "originality": {
    "score": 4,
    "positive": "Combines family-specific compatibility, explicit metric definitions, and evidence-grounded interpretation in one diagnostic contract.",
    "negative": "The description presents an integration design rather than a new recommendation architecture or diagnostic algorithm."
  },
  "future_potential": {
    "score": 8,
    "positive": "Could support reproducible diagnosis and targeted HSTU improvements while maintaining benchmark comparability.",
    "negative": "Diagnostic correlations require validation; training score margins alone cannot establish improvements in held-out HR@10."
  },
  "code_difficulty": {
    "score": 5,
    "positive": "The interface is compact and most measurements can reuse existing model features and batch tensors.",
    "negative": "Correct feature alignment, padding masks, score broadcasting, and architecture-specific probe adaptation require careful implementation."
  }
}
